Insurance

Group Life Insurance in Kenya

Group life insurance pays a benefit to an employee’s beneficiaries if the employee dies while covered, regardless of whether the death is work-related. It is a common employee benefit, usually priced and arranged for the group as a whole.

Request a quoteSpeak to an advisor

General information only. What is covered, the terms and the premium depend on the insurer’s policy wording, your circumstances and the information you disclose. Nothing here is a promise of cover.

What it covers

  • Death benefit, commonly expressed as a multiple of annual salary
  • Optional extensions such as funeral expenses, where offered
  • Disability and critical illness riders on some schemes

Who needs it

  • Employers building an employee benefits package
  • Schools, NGOs and SACCOs
  • Organisations required by contract to provide life cover

Common risks

Benefits out of date

Salary increases can leave cover too low.

Important considerations and exclusions

  • Eligibility and free cover limits apply.
  • Exclusions apply, for example for certain causes of death.

What affects the premium

  • Number of employees
  • Salary roll
  • Benefit multiple
  • Age profile

Premiums are set by insurers, so we do not publish figures. Tell us about your situation and we will explain what is driving the quotation.

What we need for a quotation

  • Employee numbers and salary roll
  • Benefit multiple wanted
  • Existing scheme details

How Chestnut can help

We explain the cover in plain language, collect the information insurers need, approach suitable insurers for terms, and help with renewals and claims. Policies are issued by insurers, and you decide what to buy.

Frequently asked questions

Is group life the same as WIBA?

No. Group life pays on death from most causes. WIBA addresses work injury and disease. Employers often have both.
